name: Central bank stress
value: Fed Dec rise priced ~89%; BoE signals more
summary: Markets fully price a December Fed rise after hot October CPI; Bank of England says a further rise is likely
state: After October CPI beat forecasts, Fed Governor Waller said on 10 Nov he would back a December rise and that a half-point move could be warranted; CME FedWatch showed about an 89% chance of a quarter-point rise and 11% of a half-point (MPA, 10 Nov). The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov and Governor Bailey said another rise is likely unless the Middle East conflict is resolved (Reuters via Express Tribune). Central banks face a stagflationary dilemma; no emergency inter-meeting move was found as of 14 Nov.
for_you: Rising policy rates feed through to mortgage, loan and credit-card costs in the US and UK, while savings rates tend to rise. Borrowers on variable rates or nearing the end of fixed deals are the most exposed.
rubric_hit: Watch: stagflationary dilemma with rate rises into high inflation; no emergency inter-meeting move (Alert)

sources.title: MPA — Fed rate hike odds hit 100% as Waller floats bigger December move
Express Tribune (Reuters) — Bank of England raises rates for first time since 2023, says more may come

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
